text:
maria: Quick q — UX asks if we should expose a "compatibility mode" toggle in Console that forces V1 routing (for legacy customers). Current behavior is automatic fallbacks via header negotiation.
aj: why would they need a toggle vs relying on header?
sven: some customers want explicit pinning for audits, also easier to correlate billing.
maria: exactly. Product wants a visible switch + telemetry flag so support can verify.
jamal: operational concern: if we surface a toggle that forces V1, we need throttling/quota mapping so it doesn't bypass v2 limits.
tayler: +1. Also need to show an advisory: "V1 is deprecated — use only for emergency rollback". Maybe a soft-warning banner. :warning:
aj: implementation notes:
- Console toggle writes customer metadata: `compat_mode: v1` in control plane
- Router respects metadata header `x-rw-compat: v1` and routes accordingly
- Telemetry should emit `compat_toggle.set` event

sven: sample header negotiation fallback we currently use:
```
if (x-rw-version) route to requested;
else try v2;
if (v2 capacity == overloaded) fallback to v1 variant;
```
If we add forced toggle, router should short-circuit to v1 before trying v2.

jamal: capacity/quotas: we already decouple v1/v2 quotas per account. Forced pin should still consume the v2 reserved if user has V2 reserved capacity? that could be confusing.
aj: proposal: forced v1 consumes v1 quota; if customer has only v2 reserved capacity, we display guidance and block toggle with a CTA to request exemptions.

maria: UX copy draft:
"Enable compatibility mode (V1): Route all requests to your account's V1 endpoints. Intended for emergency rollbacks only. V1 is deprecated and may be removed in future releases. Enabling may change your billing and quota usage."

tayler: Add a telemetry requirement: emit `compat_toggle_preview` when user hovers or opens modal, `compat_toggle_enable` on enable, and `compat_toggle_disable` on disable. Hook these to alerts if usage spikes after enabling.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary deploy of compat-toggle service v1.3 started on cluster northwest-2
maria: Who owns the console flag backend? @aj?
aj: I can own the API surface. Need an schema for the metadata change. Suggest adding `compat` object:
```
compat: {
  mode: "v1" | "auto",
  set_by: "console" | "api",
  set_at: "timestamp"
}
```
jamal: keep flat keys for easier RBAC checks `compat_mode`, `compat_set_by`, `compat_set_at` — avoid nested objects in DB row.
sven: Console should show last 7 days of route metrics when toggle is enabled (latency, error-rate-by-model), and clearly highlight increased fallbacks.

maria: Decision points before we ship:
- Block toggle if account lacks v1 quota (jamal)
- Emit 3 telemetry events (tayler)
- Router ordering: forced toggle short-circuits (sven)
- Console copy + warning (maria)

aj: I'll draft API change PR and add a feature flag `console_compat_toggle` for 2 weeks of internal dogfooding.
tayler: I'll add dashboards + alert rules: alert if error-rate increases >5% vs baseline within 30 min of toggle.

maria: timeline: PR this week, dogfood next week, opt-in beta to a few accounts after that.

jamal: one more: add an audit log entry for toggles (who did it). Compliance wants it.

sven: ACK. I'll add route-level telemetry to show what percent of traffic actually hits v1 after toggle.

maria: Thanks team. If no objections I'll move to RFC doc and PR. :thumbsup:
aj: No objections. I'll tag you in the PR when ready.
